Per: Justice Atul Sreedharan

The present appeal has been filed by the appellants, who are aggrieved by the order dated 21.10.2024 passed by the learned Single Bench in W.P No.11841 of 2017 by which the petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India by the appellants herein challenging an award dated 16.09.1994 passed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 being Land Acquisition Case No.4/A82/91-92 by Land Acquisition Officer, Bhopal.
2 . The petition relates to the acquisition of land, as already stated hereinabove, pertaining to the year 1994.

The learned Single Bench has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49223 2 WA-3098-2024 relied upon the judgement passed by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With specifically, the learned Single Bench has relied upon para 366.9 of the said judgment where the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in relation to sub-Section (4) Section 24 of the 2013 Act that did not create a new cause of action with regard to the question of legality of the proceedings already concluded under the old Act.

It further clarifies Section 24 of the new Act would only apply to Narayan Singh (Dead) Through Legal ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173462905/
1 proceedings which were pending on the date of enforcement of the new Act which came into effect from 1.1.2014. The Hon'ble Supreme Court also clarify that the new Act does not go to revive stale and time-barred claims and would not result in the reconsideration of proceedings which have already stood closed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the learned Single Bench observed that possession has been taken and compensation has been deposited with the State Government under Section 31 of the old Act and therefore, Section 24(2) of the new act would not be attracted.
3. The Court questioned the petitioner on the aspects of delay and laches in filing the petition as the cause of action arose from the award dated 16.09.1994.
In other words, the petition was filed after the delay of 20 years and therefore, the reasons for the same were sought by the learned Single Judge.

The learned Single Bench was informed that the petitioner (before the learned Single Bench)
was participating in proceedings relating to the same land which was acquired under the old Act,
under the M.P Madhya Pradesh Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act of 1976.

entities.text: M.P Madhya Pradesh Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act of 1976
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Before this Court,
the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49223 3 WA-3098-2024 learned counsel for the appellants has argued that the proceedings under the Land and Ceiling Act continued for long and infact it attained finality only after the acquisition was made in the year 1994.
This was the same argument which was also made before the Hon'ble Single Bench.

The Hon'ble Singh Bench has recorded the fact that there is no pleadings explaining delay and laches and that no pleadings were made that the pendency of Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act proceedings would have an overriding effect on the other aspects.
Before this Court also, learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the appellants had filed additional documents before the learned Single Bench and also filed an amendment application.
As regards the additional documents that have been filed

,
obviously the same cannot be considered until and unless relevant pleadings pertaining to those documents were made in the petition.
4. The primary cause for the dismissal of the writ petition is delay and laches which is more than 20 years.

Learned counsel for the appellants has argued before this Court that the dismissal of the petition on the grounds of laches of delay would having justifiable had the same been caused by the petitioner.

In this case, learned counsel for the appellants submits that he came to know of the concluded land acquisition proceedings only in the year 2017 and immediately thereafter filed the writ petition in the year 2017.
5. It is a well-settled legal principle that the law aids the vigilant, not the indolent.
This is enshrined in the maxima - "Vigilantibus non est dormientibus jura subveniunt".

No reasons have been given as to why the appellants did not take such measures which could have disclosed knowledge NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49223 4 WA-3098-2024 of the concluded land acquisition proceedings in the year 1994 itself but for a bald statement that has been made before this Court that he came to know only in the year 2017 about the concluded proceedings in 1994.
How he came to know, which are the documents he examined or was the information given to him by someone known to him, none of that has been mentioned.

6. Under the circumstances, the dismissal of the petition on the grounds of delay and laches is not perverse, therefore this Court does not find any need to interfere to the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
